paragraph: Angola's [digital lines held for both years rose 0.6 per cent in 2026](<https://cms.minfin.gov.ao/api/assets/portal-minfin/c5bb7353-28e6-4b09-9251-b8108ddbf6f9/>), from 9.85 billion kwanza for 2025 to 9.91 billion. The [communications programme fell 30.5% in the 2026 budget](<https://pti.ao/governo-corta-quase-50-da-verba-para-o-programa-de-expansao-de-internet-4g/>), to 159.2 billion kwanza. A [supplementary credit of 275 million US dollars was opened in the 2026 budget for the Ministry of Territorial Administration's citizens' database plan](<https://www.novojornal.co.ao/economia/detalhe/pr-manda-abrir-credito-adicional-suplementar-de-275-milhoes-usd-no-oge2026-para-o-mat-e-duplica-dotacao-do-ministerio-70083.html>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No fund, levy or assigned tax has been found created, collecting or paying for digital programmes. Operating would need a fund, levy or assigned tax that collected or paid, or state money put to a programme the government said the country must fund itself.

In Burundi the [digital lines held for both years total 3,236,082,542 Burundi francs for 2026/27 against 3,015,773,158 for 2025/26](<https://finances.gov.bi/index.php/2026/07/04/loi-n-1-10-du-30-juin-portant-fixation-du-budget-general-de-letat-pour-lexercice-2026-2027/>), a rise of 7.3%. The [Fonds de Service Universel des TIC is funded by a 1% levy on operators' turnover](<https://armp.gov.bi/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/PLAN_PREVISIONNEL__DE_PASSATION_DES_MARCHES_revise__2025-2026-a-publier-le_12_nov_2025.pdf>), set by decree 100/054 of 29 March 2024. Its [2026/27 plan pays 11.4 billion francs for internet connectivity to public health facilities, secondary schools and community telecentres](<https://armp.gov.bi/archives/10856>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No budget execution report, settlement law, audited accounts or fund account from the last three years has been found giving actual spending. Mature would need one of these giving what was spent, for a year from 2024.

Benin's [2026 digital budget of 27.2 billion CFA francs is 6.32% lower than the 29.034 billion approved for 2025, mainly through a 12.22% fall in external financing](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/tech/benin-cuts-digital-budget-by-6-32-despite-expanding-tech-ambitions>). By 30 April 2026 [77,247,968 francs of the Numérique programme's 12,372,151,413 had been ordered for payment](<https://budgetbenin.bj/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Note-de-presentation-du-PLFR-2026.pdf>). The ministry's 2027 draft budget [is 11.59 billion francs, against 16,483,428,674 in 2026](<https://lanation.bj/actualites/etude-du-projet-de-budget-2027-a-lassemblee-nationale-1159-milliards-f-cfa-pour-accelerer-la-transformation-digitale>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found shows the money for digital transformation higher in the latest budget than in the one before. Establishing would need that money higher in the latest budget, in the country's own currency and not adjusted for inflation.

In Burkina Faso the [digital lines held for both years total 6,174,786,000 francs for 2026 against 6,947,413,000 for 2025](<https://budgetouvert.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/loi-de-finances-pour-lexecution-du-budget-de-letat-exercice-2026.pdf>), a fall of 11.1%. The [execution report to 31 December 2025 shows the ministry's domestic investment ordered for payment at 2,094,406,682 francs](<https://budgetouvert.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/rapport-sur-la-situation-dexecution-du-budget-et-de-la-tresorerie-de-letat-exercice-2025-au-31-decembre.pdf>). On 16 April 2026 the [Council of Ministers authorised 9,113,100,000 francs of procurement for the ministry's specific projects, financed by the 2026 state budget](<https://burkina24.com/2026/04/16/compte-rendu-du-conseil-des-ministres-du-jeudi-16-avril-2026/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found shows the money for digital transformation higher in the latest budget than in the one before. Establishing would need that money higher, in the country's own currency and not adjusted for inflation.

Botswana's Ministry of Communications and Innovation has a development budget for 2026/27 of 473,200,000 pula, [down 11.5% on the revised 2025/26 figure and 44.6% on the 2025/26 appropriation](<https://www.finance.gov.bw/images/Budget-Tables/EXPENDITURE_ESTIMATES_26-27_FINAL_DRAFT.pdf>). The digital lines held for both years total [1,040,522,175 pula for 2026/27 against 1,055,985,797 for 2025/26](<https://www.finance.gov.bw/images/Budget-Tables/EXPENDITURE_ESTIMATES_26-27_FINAL_DRAFT.pdf>). [Two primary-school Digital Centres, each costing 1.59 million pula, were launched on 28 November 2025](<http://www.bocra.org.bw/sites/default/files/sites/default/files/documents/BOCRA_Newsletter%2C_Issue_003_compressed.pdf>) through the Universal Access and Service Fund Trust. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found shows the state's money for digital programmes higher in the latest budget than in the one before. Establishing would need that money higher, in the country's own currency and not adjusted for inflation.

In the Central African Republic the digital lines held for both years total [4,384,800,000 CFA francs for 2026 against 3,804,800,000 for 2025, up 15.2 per cent](<http://www.finances.gouv.cf/sites/default/files/2025-11/Projet%20de%20Loi%20de%20Finances%202026%20Version%20AN.pdf>). The 2026 draft proposes [300,000,000 CFA francs from domestic financing for urban optical fibre loops](<http://www.finances.gouv.cf/sites/default/files/2026-03/Cadre%20des%20D%C3%A9penses%20%C3%A0%20Moyen%20Terme%202026.pdf>). The 2025 finance bill carried [1,400,000,000 CFA francs of domestic money in support of the regulator ARCEP](<http://www.finances.gouv.cf/sites/default/files/2024-12/3-%20PLF2025%2004%2012%202024.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No fund, levy or assigned tax has been found created, collecting or paying, and no pledge to pay for digital programmes at home has been found with an act following it. No pledge to pay at home has been found with state money following it. Operating would need either.

In Côte d'Ivoire the [digital lines held for both years total 148,105,376,640 CFA francs for 2026 against 157,659,408,117 for 2025, down 6.1 per cent](<https://www.dgbf.ci/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Loi-de-Finances-2026.pdf>). The ministry [says it spent 64,613,612,862 of its 65,425,224,828 CFA franc budget for 2025](<https://telecom.gouv.ci/uploads/publications/179457122271.pdf>), 98.76%. Programme 23237 is an earmarked account funded by a levy on telecom operators, and the [2026 finance law appropriates 33 billion CFA francs to it](<https://www.dgbf.ci/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Loi-de-Finances-2026.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. The reported 37% rise in the ministry's 2026 budget gives no 2025 figure. Establishing would need the money for digital transformation higher in the latest budget than in the one before, in the country's own currency and not adjusted for inflation.

In Cameroon's tabled 2026 finance bill the digital lines held for both years total [26,500,000,000 CFA francs for 2026 against 26,000,000,000 for 2025](<https://rfp.cm/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/PROJET-DE-LOI-FINANCES-2026_FR_26112025.pdf>), up 1.9 per cent. [The budget directorate reports that in 2024 the digital ecosystem programme used 22.66 per cent of its credits and the cybersecurity programme all of them](<https://www.dgb.cm/minpostel-optimiser-le-cadre-logique-des-programmes/>). The universal service strategy validated on 8 July 2025 [calls for relaunching the special telecommunications fund](<https://patnuc.cm/2025/07/11/numerique-pour-tous-le-cameroun-valide-sa-strategie-nationale-de-service-universel/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No fund, levy or assigned tax for digital programmes has been found created, collecting or paying. No pledge to pay at home has been found with state money following it. Operating would need either.

The 2026 budget law [gives 81,698,223,741 Congolese francs of domestic money to section 71, Digital Economy](<https://www.budget.gouv.cd/wp-content/uploads/budget2026/lf_2026_depenses_final.pdf>). In the last twelve months, on 8 August 2026, the universal service fund [signed its first subsidy conventions with Vodacom, Airtel, Africell and Orange](<https://www.fdsu.cd/blog/rdc-le-fdsu-passe-du-diagnostic-a-laction-avec-les-premieres-conventions-de-subvention-pour-la-connectivite-universelle>), worth US$4,182,998 for 40 pilot sites. In February 2025 the secretary general of Internet Society RDC had [said the universal service fund was still not available](<https://actualite.cd/2025/02/19/kinshasa-des-jeunes-et-membres-de-internet-society-outilles-sur-le-bien-fonde-du-fonds>). For 2025 the provisional execution statement [shows 31,358,784,468 francs paid against a voted 60,627,481,411](<https://www.budget.gouv.cd/wp-content/uploads/budget2025/budget2025_rect/lf_2025_depenses.pdf>). How much of the fund's subsidy has been paid out to the operators has not been found.

The 2026 finance law [appropriates 30,139,589,283 CFA francs for programme 118, Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy](<https://sgg.cg/JO/2026/congo-jo-2026-3-3.pdf>), [up 30.5% from 23,093,583,163 for 2025](<https://sgg.cg/JO/2026/congo-jo-2026-3-3.pdf>). The 2025 budget execution report [gives 3,158,525,582 francs spent on the programme in 2025, excluding personnel](<https://sgg.cg/JO/2024/congo-jo-2024-15-sp.pdf>). The law also [appropriates 1,000,000,000 francs to the special account for the universal access and service fund](<https://sgg.cg/JO/2026/congo-jo-2026-3-3.pdf>). In the last twelve months, a tax on new SIM-card terminals has been [in force since 1 June 2026, and was reported operating on 16 July 2026](<https://aden.cg/2026/07/23/taxe-sur-les-nouveaux-terminaux-numeriques-a-cartes-sim-rtn-laden-fait-le-point-de-son-operationnalisation-devant-la-commission-economie-et-finances-de-lassemblee-nationale/>). The amount the tax has collected has not been found.

The 2026 finance law [appropriates 277,128,000 Comorian francs to the state information and communication directorate, up from nothing in 2025](<https://finances.gouv.km/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Decret-N26-003PR-du-16-jan-2026.pdf>). The [digital lines held for both years total 541,558,972 francs for 2026 against 444,285,104 for 2025](<https://finances.gouv.km/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Decret-N%C2%B026-003PR-du-16-jan-2026-portant-Prom-Loi-25-020AU-portant-Loi-de-Finan.pdf>). The law also [gives 50,000,000 francs as a transfer to the chambre du Numérique](<https://finances.gouv.km/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Decret-N26-003PR-du-16-jan-2026.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source from the last three years has been found showing the government saying digital transformation must be paid for from the country's own resources and acting on it. Operating would need a fund, levy or assigned tax that collected or paid, or state money put to a programme the government said the country must fund itself.

Cape Verde's digital economy ministry's [appropriation fell from 369,781,930 Cape Verdean escudos in 2025 to 174,200,533 in 2026](<https://www.mf.gov.cv/documents/198414/6576107/Mapas_Contas_1%C2%BA_Trim_%202026_Site.xlsx>). The [digital lines held for both years total 2,149,551,552 escudos for 2026 against 6,680,534,274 for 2025](<https://www.mf.gov.cv/documents/198414/5793427/Lei%20que%20aprova%20o%20OE%202026.pdf>). The 2026 budget law [earmarks the operators' communications contribution and the radio-spectrum fee to the universal service and information society fund](<https://www.mf.gov.cv/documents/198414/5793427/Lei%20que%20aprova%20o%20OE%202026.pdf>) and [appropriates 122,073,633 escudos for 2026](<https://www.mf.gov.cv/documents/198414/5793427/Lei%20que%20aprova%20o%20OE%202026.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. The amount the fund collected or paid out has not been found. Establishing would need the money for digital transformation higher in the latest budget than in the one before, in the country's own currency and not adjusted for inflation.

In Djibouti the digital lines held for both years total [485,686,344 for 2026 against 456,943,040 for 2025](<https://www.journalofficiel.dj/texte-juridique/arrete-n2026-041-pr-mefi-portant-approbation-du-projet-de-budget-previsionnel-de-linstitut-de-la-statistique-de-djibouti-instad-pour-lexercice-2026/>), a rise of 6.3 per cent in francs. The 2026 budget of ANSIE, the state digital agency, is [396.1 million Djibouti francs, down from 556.7 million in 2025](<https://www.presidence.dj/conseil-des-ministres/2025-12-30>). The nearest fact found is that [ANSIE's 2026 revenue is mainly the state subvention](<https://www.presidence.dj/conseil-des-ministres/2025-12-30>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No fund or levy has been found paying for digital programmes. Operating would need a fund, levy or assigned tax that collected or paid, or state money put to a programme the government said the country must fund itself.

Algeria's 2026 budget [gives 20,589,518,000 Algerian dinars to 10 digital lines](<https://www.joradp.dz/FTP/jo-francais/2026/F2026002.pdf>). In the last twelve months, on 7 September 2026, the regulator [launched a tender for mobile coverage of 3000 small localities](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/0809-141386-algerie-un-nouveau-pas-vers-la-generalisation-des-services-telecoms>), [financed wholly by the state through the universal service mechanism](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/0809-141386-algerie-un-nouveau-pas-vers-la-generalisation-des-services-telecoms>). The state also pays [more than 27.3 billion dinars, about 204 million dollars, through the fonds d'appui du service universel](<https://algerian-business.com/mobilis-4g-algerie-201-sites-27-milliards/>) for the 201-site Mobilis 4G programme. The money for digital transformation has not been found for two budget years running. Establishing would need that money higher in the latest budget than in the one before.

The 39 digital lines held for both years in Egypt total [30,224,315,000 pounds for 2026/27 against 24,302,193,000 for 2025/26](<https://assets.mof.gov.eg/files/75b68ce0-b031-11f1-9534-032ecbc6b98c.pdf>), a rise of 24.4%. In the last twelve months, in June 2026, the House budget committee approved [about 23.3 billion pounds for the ICT ministry's general office for 2026/27](<https://www.tafsela.net/62665>), up from 19.69 billion the year before. In the same month it approved [a transfer of about 5.7 billion pounds to the Universal Service Fund](<https://www.aldawlanews.com/1358526>) in the regulator's 2026/27 budget. No source found shows the Universal Service Fund collecting or paying in the last three years. No pledge to pay at home has been found with state money following it. Operating would need either.

Ethiopia's 2026/27 federal budget gives [35,959,539,563 birr to 125 digital lines](<https://www.mofed.gov.et/media/filer_public/c1/de/c1de6f52-b57e-4a94-91ff-cc22a2c751b8/2019_e_c_budget_year_goe_federal_budget_proclamation_part_two_updated.xlsx>). The 73 digital lines held for both years total [21,697,879,134 birr for 2026/27 against 14,643,622,841 for 2025/26](<https://www.mofed.gov.et/media/filer_public/c1/de/c1de6f52-b57e-4a94-91ff-cc22a2c751b8/2019_e_c_budget_year_goe_federal_budget_proclamation_part_two_updated.xlsx>), a rise of 48.2%. In 2024/25 the Ministry of Innovation and Technology [was voted 2,754,552,330 birr and spent 989,820,128, or 35.9%](<https://www.mofed.gov.et/media/filer_public/c1/de/c1de6f52-b57e-4a94-91ff-cc22a2c751b8/2019_e_c_budget_year_goe_federal_budget_proclamation_part_two_updated.xlsx>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No fund, levy or assigned tax has been found created, collecting or paying for digital programmes. Operating would need a fund, levy or assigned tax that collected or paid, or state money put to a programme the government said the country must fund itself.

Gabon's 2026 budget document is dated 17 July 2026. It shows digital lines held for both years totalling [25,152,318,272 CFA francs for 2026 against 22,855,429,916 for 2025](<https://www.dgb-gabon.net/uploads/documentation/Texte%20juridique/178593988623.pdf>), a rise of 10.0 per cent. In the last twelve months, the 2027 finance bill was presented to the National Assembly on 25 October 2026. It [asks 37,214,804,386 CFA francs for the Ministry of the Digital Economy, against 53,711,081,266 in 2026](<https://agpgabon.ga/gabon-loi-de-finances-2027-les-budgets-de-la-communication-et-de-leconomie-numerique-examines-a-lassemblee-nationale/>), a fall of about 16.5 billion. No fund, levy or assigned tax for digital programmes has been found created, collecting or paying, and no spending figure has been found. Establishing would need that money higher in the latest budget than in the one before.

In the 2026 budget Ghana's digital lines held for both years total [258,438,014 cedis for 2026 against 42,313,121 for 2025](<https://mofep.gov.gh/sites/default/files/pbb-estimates/2026/2026-PBB-MOCD.pdf>), a rise of 510.8 per cent. The Appropriation (No. 2) Act, 2025 [appropriates 100,000,000 cedis for the ICT Capacity Development programme](<https://www.mofep.gov.gh/sites/default/files/budget-statements/Appropriation%20%28%20No.%202%29%20Act%2C%202025%20Act%201163_0.pdf>) of the Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations for 2026, wholly from domestic revenue. The [Cyber Security Authority sub-programme receives 25,346,198 cedis](<https://mofep.gov.gh/sites/default/files/pbb-estimates/2026/2026-PBB-MOCD.pdf>) for 2026. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No fund, levy or assigned tax has been found created, collecting or paying, and no spending figure has been found. No pledge to pay at home has been found with state money following it. Operating would need either.

In the 2025 budget, Guinea's digital lines held for both years total [13,441,441,299 Guinean francs for 2025 against 6,758,097,055 for 2024](<https://mbudget.gov.gn/wp-content/uploads/loi-de-finance-2025.pdf>), a rise of 98.9 per cent. The budget law is dated 31 December 2024. In the last twelve months, a decree signed by President Doumbouya on 21 May 2026 [created the Digital Sovereignty Fund](<https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-digital/2605-55916-guinea-introduces-3-tax-on-foreign-digital-services>). It is to be financed mainly by a new 3 per cent Digital Compliance Fee on foreign digital services, enforced after a six-month transition. No money has been reported collected or paid. No budget execution report, settlement law, audited accounts or fund account from the last three years has been found giving actual spending. Mature would need one of these giving what was spent, for a year from 2024.

In the 2026 budget the Gambia's digital lines held for both years total [537,355,897 dalasi for 2026 against 511,618,456 for 2025](<https://mofea.gov.gm/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Final-Approved-2026-Budget-5.1.26-V2.pdf>), a rise of 5.0 per cent. In all, [24 digital lines receive 661,855,897 dalasi in 2026](<https://mofea.gov.gm/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Final-Approved-2026-Budget-5.1.26-V2.pdf>). The budget document is dated 5 January 2026 and names no fund, levy or assigned tax for them. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No execution report, settlement law or audited account has been found giving what was spent in 2024 or later. Operating would need a fund, levy or assigned tax that collected or paid, or state money put to a programme the government said the country must fund itself.

Guinea-Bissau's [2026 budget gives 129,000,000 CFA francs to six digital lines](<https://www.mef.gw/publicacoes/orcamento-geral-do-estado/2026-oge2026/viewdocument/195>). The digital lines held for both years [total 70,000,000 CFA francs for 2026 against 130,000,000 for 2025](<https://www.mef.gw/publicacoes/orcamento-geral-do-estado/2026-oge2026/viewdocument/195>), a fall of 46.2 per cent. The [budget document is dated 1 December 2025](<https://www.mef.gw/publicacoes/orcamento-geral-do-estado/2026-oge2026/viewdocument/195>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No spending figure has been found, and nothing found states a fund, levy or assigned tax paying for digital programmes. Establishing would need that money higher in the latest budget than in the one before, in the country's own currency and not adjusted for inflation.

Equatorial Guinea's [budget law is dated 9 December 2025](<https://minhacienda-gob.com/uploads/2026/05/libro-lpge-2026-bcb5ebfc7795.pdf>). The [2026 budget gives 23,476,749,000 Central African CFA francs to 113 digital lines](<https://minhacienda-gob.com/uploads/2026/05/libro-lpge-2026-bcb5ebfc7795.pdf>). The ten lines held for both years [total 8,528,000,000 for 2026 against 8,668,000,000 for 2025](<https://minhacienda-gob.com/uploads/2026/05/libro-lpge-2026-bcb5ebfc7795.pdf>), a fall of 1.6 per cent. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No execution report, settlement law or audited account has been found giving what was spent in 2024 or later, and no fund or levy has been found. Establishing would need that money higher in the latest budget than in the one before, in the country's own currency and not adjusted for inflation.

The [2026/27 budget appropriates KES 12,763,784,217 to the State Department for ICT and Digital Economy](<https://www.treasury.go.ke/sites/default/files/Budget%20Books/Budget%20books%202026-2027/FY%202026%202027%20Programme%20Based%20Budget%20Book.pdf>). The [digital lines held for both years total 43,931,556,738 shillings for 2026/27 against 37,618,002,025 for 2025/26](<https://treasury.go.ke/sites/default/files/Budget%20Books/Budget%20books%202026-2027/FY%202026%202027%20Programme%20Based%20Budget%20Book_Approved.pdf>), a rise of 16.8 per cent. The Communications Authority's annual report [gives 14.69 billion shillings spent by the Authority and its Universal Service Fund in 2024/25](<https://www.ca.go.ke/sites/default/files/2026-07/Annual%20Report%20FY%202024-2025.pdf>). The Universal Service Fund [funded the Digital Superhighway backbone and metro fibre procurement](<https://www.pulse.co.ke/story/ag-opinion-clearing-sh15bn-digital-superhighway-tender-quashed-2026090416090271184>). In the last twelve months, in August 2026, it also funded [a skilling project for 120,000 people across 19 counties](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/08/19/kenya-targets-120000-people-for-digital-skills-training-across-19-counties/>).

Liberia's [FY2026 budget gives 12,464,422 US dollars to 14 digital lines](<https://mfdp.gov.lr/uploads/documents/2026/09/fy2026-national-budget.pdf>). The Liberia Telecommunications Authority [created the Universal Access Fund by regulation on 10 September 2015, with licensee contributions of 0.5 per cent of annual gross revenues for its first year](<https://lta.gov.lr/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/Regulations-on-the-Universal-Access-Fund-LTA-REG-0006-.pdf>). On 20 October 2025 the fund [reported installing Starlink in Vahun District, Lofa County](<https://universalaccessfund.com/starlink-installed-in-vahun-district-to-boost-internet-access-in-rural-liberia/>), with no cost given. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found gives the digital money in two budget years running, so no source found says whether it rose. Establishing would need that money higher in the latest budget than in the one before, in the country's own currency and not adjusted for inflation.

Libya's 2025 budget gives [1,127,365,400 Libyan dinars to 36 digital lines](<https://lawsociety.ly/legislation/%D9%85%D8%B4%D8%B1%D9%88%D8%B9-%D8%B1%D9%82%D9%85-1-%D9%84%D8%B3%D9%86%D8%A9-2025-%D9%85-%D8%A8%D8%B4%D8%A3%D9%86-%D9%82%D8%A7%D9%86%D9%88%D9%86-%D8%A7%D8%B9%D8%AA%D9%85%D8%A7%D8%AF-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85/>). The digital lines held for both years [total 1,064,321,200 dinars for 2025 against 1,064,321,200 for 2024](<https://lawsociety.ly/legislation/%D9%85%D8%B4%D8%B1%D9%88%D8%B9-%D8%B1%D9%82%D9%85-1-%D9%84%D8%B3%D9%86%D8%A9-2025-%D9%85-%D8%A8%D8%B4%D8%A3%D9%86-%D9%82%D8%A7%D9%86%D9%88%D9%86-%D8%A7%D8%B9%D8%AA%D9%85%D8%A7%D8%AF-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85/>). The fund is paid by a levy of 2% of operators' gross annual revenue. In the last twelve months, in 2026, ATC Uganda [paid 20.9 billion shillings into the fund](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/08/05/atc-uganda-contributes-ugx-20-9-billion-to-advance-digital-inclusion/>). On 29 September 2026 the Uganda Communications Commission [sought a partner to run Phase III of the National e-Booster Programme](<https://pmldaily.com/news/2026/09/ucc-seeks-partner-to-accelerate-local-ict-innovations-under-third-e-booster-phase.html>) through the fund for 2026/27.

South Africa's digital lines held for both years [total 8,082.2 million rand for 2026/27 against 7,685.6 million for 2025/26](<https://www.treasury.gov.za/documents/National%20Budget/2026/ene/FullENE.pdf>). The 2026 Estimates raise the digital and postal access subprogramme [from 742.9 million rand in 2025/26 to 767.2 million for 2026/27](<https://www.treasury.gov.za/documents/National%20Budget/2026/ene/Vote%2030%20Communications%20and%20Digital%20Technologies.pdf>). In the last twelve months, the Universal Service and Access Fund's own figures, given in a ministerial reply, [show 1,087.9 million rand spent in 2025/26](<https://pmg.org.za/committee-question/41023/>). ICASA [collected 281.2 million rand for it in 2025/26](<https://pmg.org.za/committee-question/41023/>), and the fund has not been abolished. The 2026 Estimates [put 146.0 million rand of 2026/27 towards the universal service and access bodies](<https://www.treasury.gov.za/documents/National%20Budget/2026/ene/Vote%2030%20Communications%20and%20Digital%20Technologies.pdf>).

In Zambia the digital lines held for both years [total 1,792.9 million kwacha for 2026 against 1,594.5 million for 2025](<https://www.mofnp.gov.zm/?wpdmpro=2026-national-budget>), a rise. The Appropriation Act, 2025 [authorises 1.15 billion kwacha for Smart Zambia e-government for 2026](<https://www.parliament.gov.zm/sites/default/files/documents/acts/Act%20%20No.%2028%20of%202025%2C%20The%20Appropriation%20Act.pdf>). In the last twelve months, in May 2026, the minister [announced approval of 255 million kwacha to upgrade digital infrastructure](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/05/15/zambia-approves-k255-million-to-upgrade-digital-infrastructure-and-network-quality/>), mainly in rural areas. The budget document names no fund, levy or assigned tax for digital programmes, and none has been found created, collecting or paying. No pledge to pay at home has been found with state money following it. Operating would need either.

Zimbabwe's Budget Statement [gives the ICT ministry's Vote 23 budget as 763.5 million Zimbabwe Gold for 2026](<https://www.veritaszim.net/sites/veritas_d/files/Appropriation%20Act%202026%2C%20Act%20No.%206%20of%202025.pdf>), against 741 million for 2025, a rise of about 3 per cent. The digital lines held for both years [total 4,503.5 million Zimbabwe dollars for 2026 against 5,703.9 million for 2025](<https://zimtreasury.co.zw/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Approved-2026-Estimates-of-Expenditure.pdf>), 21.0 per cent lower. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No figure for what was spent has been found, and no fund, levy or assigned tax has been found created, collecting or paying. No pledge to pay at home has been found with state money following it. Operating would need either.
